bands.label: Strong
bands.blurb: Solid contracts, transparent operations, and an easy start.

providers.name: PortOne
providers.description: PortOne (formerly Iamport) is a Korea-based payment orchestration platform that lets online businesses integrate one API to reach 100+ Korean and global payment methods and PSPs. The V2 REST API (api.portone.io) covers payments, billing keys, scheduled/recurring payments, identity verification, cash receipts, B2B tax invoices, and partner settlement, with the legacy V1 API still served at api.iamport.kr.

bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: TheCarApi
providers.description: A multi-source vehicle auction inventory REST/JSON API aggregating live and archived auction listings and European retail classifieds. Provides search, facets, catalog, auction detail & price history, VIN history, market intelligence, and import cost calculators. Fully specified via OpenAPI 3.1 with Postman collection and agent-native documentation (llms.txt).

providers.name: Seoul National University
providers.description: Seoul National University (SNU) is South Korea's flagship national research university, a national university corporation in Seoul ranked in the QS World top 40 and identified by ROR as https://ror.org/04h9pn542. Like most universities it is a federation of buyers rather than a producer of APIs: it operates no developer portal, no open-data portal, no API gateway, no official GitHub organization, and no OAuth or OIDC authorization server. It publishes no API documentation of any kind, and every contract in this repository was written from live probing rather than from something SNU wrote. What it does operate — verified on its own hosts and its own address block on 2026-08-19 — is four machine-readable surfaces. Two OAI-PMH 2.0 data providers: S-Space, the SNU Open Repository and Archive (DSpace 5.5, content from 2008, twelve metadata formats, 100+ sets, three harvesting contexts including OpenAIRE and DRIVER), and KOSSDA, the Korea Social Science Data Archive (DSpace 5.6, content from 2017). An OpenSearch 1.1 search interface over S-Space. And a SAML 2.0 Identity Provider, entityID https://kafegw.snu.ac.kr/idp/simplesamlphp, registered in the KAFE national federation and exported into eduGAIN with REFEDS Research & Scholarship support and a Sirtfi assurance assertion — the single most consequential programmable surface the institution runs, and one no catalog had recorded. Two honest limits belong in the same breath. The repository hosts front everything except OAI-PMH with a JavaScript bot challenge that returns HTTP 200 and an HTML shell to any machine client, so the OpenSearch interface is gated rather than open. And SNU's library discovery runs on Ex Libris Alma and Primo under institution code 82SNU — real, but a tenancy, recorded below as such and never scored as SNU's engineering.

providers.name: SK Telecom
providers.description: SK Telecom Co., Ltd. is South Korea's largest mobile network operator, headquartered at SK T-Tower in Jung-gu, Seoul, and the telecom arm of SK Group. It runs the country's largest 5G and LTE network, sells fixed broadband and IPTV through subsidiary SK Broadband, operates the T world retail and care channel, and has repositioned itself as an "AI company" around its A.X sovereign Korean LLM family, the NUGU voice assistant, and the A. (A dot) assistant. Its position in the telecom value chain is that of a facilities-based incumbent carrier: it owns the radio access network, spectrum, SIM base, and identity rails that the rest of the Korean digital economy authenticates against. Its API posture is split in an unusual way. SK Telecom does run a genuine, self-serve public developer portal — SK open API at openapi.sk.com, operated by SK Telecom Co., Ltd. — but what it publishes there is AI, big-data and mobility product APIs (speech synthesis, face recognition, congestion and floating-population analytics, video analysis), not network APIs. The legacy T developers subdomains developer.sktelecom.com and developers.sktelecom.com both resolve in DNS to 211.188.149.18 and refuse connections on port 443 — a dead developer programme with dangling hostnames. On the network-API side SK Telecom is a named CAMARA participant and appears in the CAMARA landscape as an operator, has an organisation page in GSMA's Open Gateway directory, signed a domestic MoU with KT and LG Uplus in October 2024 to standardise six network APIs through Korea's TTA, endorsed the Bridge Alliance API Exchange, and signed an MoU with Aduna through subsidiary SK telink in September 2025 — but no CAMARA endpoint (Number Verification, SIM Swap, KYC Match, Quality on Demand) is callable from any SK Telecom-operated developer portal. Developers who want SK Telecom network capability reach it through aggregators — Bridge Alliance BAEx on Singtel's Paragon platform, surfaced through Nokia's Network as Code developer portal, or Aduna — not from SK Telecom directly.

providers.name: Payple
providers.description: Payple (페이플) is a South Korean payment gateway (PG) and fintech provider that lets merchants accept online payments across domestic and international cards, real-time bank-account payments, recurring / billing-key charges, link payments, identity verification, and settlement / payout (Hub) services. Integration is offered through a hosted payment window initialized in the browser with a public client key, plus a server-side REST API (v2) authorized with partner credentials (PCD_CST_ID / PCD_CUST_KEY). Payple is a registered Korean electronic financial business with an Innovative Financial Service (혁신금융서비스) designation, and it publishes official language sample source, policy documents, and a developer center. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the Payple developer center and the PAYPLECORP GitHub organization.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Korbit
providers.description: Korbit is South Korea's first cryptocurrency exchange, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Seoul, offering KRW-denominated spot trading of bitcoin, ether and other digital assets to Korean retail and institutional customers. Korbit publishes the Korbit Open API v2, a REST and WebSocket interface covering market data (tickers, orderbook, trades, candlesticks, tick-size policy), order placement and cancellation, order and trade history, balances, cryptocurrency deposit-address management and withdrawals, and KRW deposit/withdrawal push notifications. Authentication is by API key (X-KAPI-KEY) with per-request HMAC-SHA256 or ED25519 signatures, granular key permissions and optional IP allowlisting. Korbit is unusually agent-forward for an exchange: it ships an official Go CLI with a bundled MCP server and Agent Skill, a documented llms.txt, and a downloadable local sandbox that mocks the full REST and WebSocket surface for no-risk development.

providers.name: Barogo
providers.description: Barogo (바로고) is a South Korean last-mile delivery platform founded in 2014 and headquartered in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. It operates a nationwide two-wheeler dispatch network for food and goods, with rider, merchant and hub-manager apps and a store POS program, and counts McDonald's, Burger King, KFC, Krispy Kreme, Baskin Robbins and Dunkin among its clients. Its developer-facing product is Gorela (고릴라), a delivery-brokerage platform that sits between an "order agency" — a POS, marketplace or commerce platform that takes the customer's order — and the delivery agencies that assign riders. The Gorela API covers fare quoting and serviceability, order intake in fixed-fare and flexible-fare modes, order read/amend/cancel, store mapping, prepaid store balances, delivery-agency status and delivery zones, plus twenty callbacks pushed back to the partner as an order fans out into its child deliveries.

providers.name: Toss Payments
providers.description: Toss Payments is a South Korean payment gateway (PG) operated by Viva Republica, the company behind the Toss super-app. Its REST API lets merchants accept and manage online payments across cards, Korean easy-pay wallets (Toss Pay, KakaoPay, Naver Pay), virtual accounts, bank transfer, and mobile-phone billing. The Core API (base https://api.tosspayments.com) covers payment confirmation and cancellation, recurring billing keys, virtual account issuance, cash receipts, transaction and settlement queries, and seller payouts, with asynchronous results delivered by webhooks. Authentication is HTTP Basic using a secret API key.

providers.name: Sungkyunkwan University
providers.description: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) is a private research university in Seoul and Suwon, South Korea, founded in 1398 and operated since 1996 under the Samsung Foundation of Education. Like almost every university it is a federation of buyers rather than an API producer, and this profile is deliberate about which of that federation's surfaces are actually SKKU's engineering. SKKU operates no central developer portal and no API gateway — api.skku.edu, developer.skku.edu, data.skku.edu and status.skku.edu do not resolve — and publishes no OpenAPI for anything. What it does operate, and what almost no university catalog records, is a SAML 2.0 identity provider at kafe.skku.edu registered in eduGAIN through KAFE, the Korea Access Federation: entityID https://kafe.skku.edu/idp/simplesamlphp, scope skku.edu, supporting the REFEDS Research and Scholarship entity category and asserting the REFEDS Sirtfi assurance profile. That machine-readable metadata document is the strongest programmable surface SKKU runs. Its research information portal at pure.skku.edu looks institutional and is not: it CNAMEs to skku.elsevierpure.com and its OAI-PMH provider self-identifies as "Pure OAI Repository" with adminEmail purehosted@elsevier.com, so the live, conformant OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint there is recorded as an Elsevier Pure TENANCY — SKKU's data on Elsevier's contract — and no Pure specification is saved in this repository. The thesis repository at skku.dcollection.net is likewise a KERIS dCollection tenancy whose robots.txt disallows all crawling and whose OAI paths return an HTML shell. Two SKKU units are Crossref members in their own right (School of Medicine, prefix 10.23838; Institute of Legal Studies, prefix 10.17008) and the institution is registered in ROR as 04q78tk20; no DataCite provider or client exists. Everything else — Kingo Portal SSO, iCampus, course registration at sugang.skku.edu, the library discovery layer — is enrolment-gated with no public API, no developer registration and no published rate limits.

providers.name: Mindlogic
providers.description: Mindlogic is a South Korean generative-AI company whose products include FactChat (a multi-LLM enterprise chat platform with Studio chatbot building, deep research, meeting notes, and image/video generation), Bliss (a persona chatbot that learns a person's voice and personality for fan engagement), and Informe (a multilingual document-grounded website chatbot). For developers, Mindlogic operates the FactChat API Gateway — a unified, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM proxy that fronts models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, xAI and Perplexity behind a single API key, metered in credits, with chat completions, an OpenAI Responses pass-through, an Anthropic Messages pass-through, text-to-speech, and image/video generation.

providers.name: Bithumb
providers.description: Bithumb is South Korea's leading cryptocurrency exchange platform offering REST and WebSocket APIs for spot trading across KRW, BTC, and USDT markets. The APIs cover market data, order management, account management, deposit and withdrawal operations, and real-time streaming for 396+ cryptocurrencies.

providers.name: Pohang University of Science and Technology
providers.description: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) is a private research university in Pohang, North Gyeongsang, South Korea, founded in 1986 by the steelmaker POSCO and consistently ranked inside the QS world top 100. POSTECH operates no developer portal, no open-data program and no API it authored itself — but it is not empty, and three genuinely institution-operated machine-readable surfaces were verified live on 2026-08-30, all of them on POSTECH's own network (141.223.0.0/16). The OASIS institutional repository serves a fully anonymous OAI-PMH 2.0 harvesting endpoint over a corpus of 106,805 records in twelve metadata formats across 163 sets, reaching back to 2014. POSTECH runs its own SAML 2.0 identity provider at idpass.postech.ac.kr, registered in the KAFE federation since 2017 and resolvable through eduGAIN, supporting the REFEDS Research and Scholarship entity category and asserting SIRTFI — machine-readable institutional infrastructure that almost nothing in this cohort catalogues. And POSTECH's LMS publishes a live, public LTI 1.3 Advantage platform keyset and OAuth 2.0 token endpoint, which most institution-hosted Moodles keep unreachable. Everything else is a login wall or someone else's platform: the PODIUM portal, admissions and certificate systems are gated; the DSpace REST interface sits behind a JavaScript bot challenge that returns 200 with a challenge shell; and the thesis pipeline runs through postech.dcollection.net, a tenancy on the KERIS-operated national dCollection platform, recorded here as a relationship rather than as POSTECH's engineering.

providers.name: Kurly
providers.description: Kurly (컬리, operated by The Farmers Front) is a South Korean online grocery and lifestyle commerce company, known for Market Kurly and its overnight "dawn delivery" (샛별배송) model built on a cold-chain fulfillment network. Kurly Logistics Services (KLS) opens that network to contracted shipper clients (화주사) as a B2B Open API spanning three service families: fulfillment (물류대행), where Kurly holds and ships the shipper's stock, covering goods master, inbound receiving, inventory and ledgers, outbound orders and fulfillment plans; delivery agency (배송대행), where the shipper ships from their own warehouse over Kurly's Nextmile last-mile network; and shared delivery tracking. Access is contract-gated — clientId and secretKey are issued only after IP allowlist registration — and Kurly states as policy that KLS does not push data to external systems, so integrations poll rather than subscribe to webhooks.

providers.name: Kakao
providers.description: Kakao Corp. is the South Korean technology group behind KakaoTalk — the dominant mobile messenger in Korea — along with KakaoPay (payments), Kakao Bank (digital bank), KakaoMobility (taxi, navigation, parking), KakaoMap, Kakao Games, Kakao Entertainment (Melon, Kakao Webtoon, Daum), and KakaoCloud. Kakao runs its public developer platform at developers.kakao.com, exposing REST APIs for Kakao Login (OAuth 2.0), Kakao Sync, KakaoTalk Share / Message / Friend Picker / Channel, KakaoStory, KakaoNavi, KakaoMap, Local search, Daum Search, KakaoPay (PG / online easy-pay), and KoGPT generative AI. KakaoMobility and Kakao Enterprise / KakaoCloud each operate additional partner- facing developer surfaces.

providers.name: Dunamu
providers.description: Dunamu Inc. (두나무 주식회사) is a South Korean fintech and blockchain company founded in April 2012 and headquartered at 369 Gangnam-daero, Seocho-gu, Seoul. Dunamu operates Upbit, Korea's largest digital asset exchange (launched 2017, the country's first registered VASP), and Stockplus, a securities trading application launched in 2014, alongside Stockplus Unlisted for pre-IPO share trading. The group also spun out Lambda256 (blockchain infrastructure, now trading as Nodit) in 2019 and runs the Dunamu & Partners venture arm. Dunamu itself publishes no developer program at dunamu.com — its entire public API surface is served under the Upbit brand through the Upbit Developer Center, which offers REST and WebSocket APIs for market data, orders, accounts, deposits, withdrawals and Travel Rule compliance, plus first-party Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs, a CLI and packaged agent skills published from the upbit-official GitHub organization. That API surface is catalogued separately at the Upbit provider profile; this record profiles the corporate parent.

providers.name: Hanyang University
providers.description: Hanyang University is a private research university in Seoul and Ansan (ERICA), South Korea, ROR https://ror.org/046865y68. Unusually for this cohort it operates a genuine, institution-built API programme rather than a set of vendor tenancies: the HYU Open API Developer Center at api.hanyang.ac.kr publishes REST endpoints returning XML or JSON across twelve service categories (academic records, campus life, administration, research, careers, library, alumni giving, volunteering and more), backed by its own OAuth 2.0 authorization server, Android and iOS SDKs, an API console, a developer community and a full published error-code table. The catch is that the API catalogue itself is member-only: /api/search.page renders an empty template to anonymous visitors and app keys are issued only after manual administrator approval, so no endpoint list, scope list or machine-readable contract is publicly enumerable. The one openly callable institution-operated API is the OAI-PMH 2.0 interface on Hanyang's own DSpace repository at repository.hanyang.ac.kr, which answers Identify, ListMetadataFormats and ListSets correctly but returned noRecordsMatch to every harvest request probed. Its research-output and thesis surfaces are vendor tenancies (ScholarWorks/Bwise, KERIS dCollection), it registers DOIs through eight institute-level Crossref memberships rather than centrally, and it publishes no SAML identity-provider metadata to KAFE or eduGAIN while eleven of its Korean peers do.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: My Real Trip
providers.description: My Real Trip (마이리얼트립) is South Korea's largest online travel platform, founded in 2012, selling flights, stays, tours, tickets, and activities across 680+ cities in 80+ countries to roughly 5 million monthly active users. For developers it publishes a Partner API (partner-ext-api.myrealtrip.com) that lets marketing/affiliate partners search products, generate trackable MyLink short links, and pull revenue and reservation reports, secured with a Bearer API key. It also operates an official public Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes real-time flight, stay, and tour/activity search to AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.

providers.name: Toss
providers.description: Toss is a Korean financial super-app operated by Viva Republica that provides REST APIs for payments, banking, credit scoring, identity verification, and financial services across the Toss ecosystem. The Toss Payments platform supports card payments, virtual accounts, mobile phone billing, bank transfers, and digital wallets including TossPay, KakaoPay, NaverPay, and SamsungPay, serving over 30 million registered users across South Korea.

providers.name: Coupang
providers.description: Coupang is a South Korean e-commerce company offering rapid delivery of a wide range of products including groceries, electronics, fashion, and household goods through its mobile app and website. Coupang exposes an Open API platform for marketplace sellers (vendors) to integrate product catalog, order, return, cancellation, settlement, and inquiry workflows.

providers.name: KakaoBank
providers.description: KakaoBank is South Korea's leading internet-only bank, offering REST APIs for account management, fund transfers, loans, credit scoring, and open banking data connectivity for the Korean market. Founded in 2016 and backed by Kakao Corp., KakaoBank serves over 26 million customers through a fully mobile and API-first digital banking platform.

providers.name: PUBLY
providers.description: PUBLY is a Korean career-development and content membership platform operated by NEWNEEK Co., Ltd. (뉴닉). It offers a subscription-based Career Membership giving working professionals access to curated career content, series, templates and job-transition guides, personalized daily recommendations by career stage, an AI feature (Perdy, beta), and a newsletter. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; PUBLY publishes a consumer web product and does not expose a public developer API, so this profile carries identity and security-posture signal only.

providers.name: Tridge
providers.description: Tridge is a South Korea-headquartered global agri-food trade intelligence and sourcing platform. It combines a data layer of structured cross-border trade, price, production, seasonality and weather data (the company cites 682M+ trade data points and 65M+ price records across 200+ markets), a network layer of verified buyers and suppliers in 190+ countries, and an AI layer that runs trade workflows from discovery through deal closure. Products include Market Curations, Sourcing Hub, Data & Analytics, Tridge Eye (market intelligence) and Tridge Ark (AI-driven export sales outreach). Tridge advertises an API for integrating its global price and trade data into customer systems, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation or machine-readable contract — access is arranged through a sales conversation.

providers.name: Naver
providers.description: Naver Corp. is South Korea's largest internet company, operating the Naver search portal, Naver Webtoon, Naver Pay, Naver Maps, Naver Shopping, WORKS Mobile, and the LINE messenger platform (jointly with SoftBank via LY Corporation). Naver runs two distinct public developer surfaces: Naver Developers (developers.naver.com) which hosts Naver's classic Open APIs — Search (blog, news, book, encyclopedia, café, knowledge, web, image, shop, doc), Papago N2MT translation, Naver Login (OAuth 2.0), Naver Maps geocoding and static map, Datalab trend, CAPTCHA, and SmartEditor; and Naver Cloud Platform (www.ncloud.com) — Naver's IaaS / PaaS offering with Compute (Server, Container, Functions), Storage (Object, Block, File), Network (VPC, CDN+, Global Edge), AI (CLOVA Speech, CLOVA OCR, Papago, HyperCLOVA X), Maps, SENS (SMS / push messaging), Cloud Search, and Certificate Manager.

providers.name: Yonsei University
providers.description: Yonsei University (연세대학교) is a private research university in Seoul, South Korea, founded in 1885 and one of the "SKY" institutions. Its programmable footprint is small, and most of what previously appeared under its name was not its own engineering: the Yonsei Research Information portal at yonsei.elsevierpure.com is an Elsevier Pure (CRIS) tenancy whose OpenAPI is authored by Elsevier — info.title "Pure API", contact pure-support@elsevier.com — and whose data endpoints and OAI-PMH feed both return HTTP 401 to the public. That relationship is recorded here as a tenant surface; the contract itself belongs to Elsevier and has been removed from this repo. What Yonsei genuinely operates is narrower and more interesting: a SAML 2.0 Identity Provider on its own domain (kafe.yonsei.ac.kr) registered in the Korean Access FEderation and exported to eduGAIN with the scope yonsei.ac.kr and a Sirtfi declaration; a DSpace 5.5 medical-library repository (YUHSpace) at ir.ymlib.yonsei.ac.kr serving public RSS 2.0 and Atom 1.0 feeds from behind a JavaScript bot challenge, with no OAI-PMH deployed; and a members-only Yonsei Data Portal at data.yonsei.ac.kr that ships no public API. There is no central developer portal, no institution-operated REST API, and no official institutional GitHub organization — the only GitHub presence is GDGoC Yonsei, a student Google Developer Group. The institutional AI posture is a governance document, not an API, and it exists only on the Korean surface.

providers.name: Simpatico Project
providers.description: Simpatico Project (유쾌한프로젝트, Yukwaehan Project Co., Ltd.) is a Korean B2B mental-wellness startup, backed by 500 Global, whose product Clify (클라이피, "Climb & Clarify") is an AI-based integrated mental-care and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) solution for individuals and companies. Clify uses a patented multimodal algorithm to fuse Face & Voice biosignals — blood-flow changes, micro-expressions and voice characteristics — into a roughly one-minute mental-state diagnosis (stress, anxiety, depression, burnout) that it claims exceeds 90% accuracy, and rolls the results up into an organization insight dashboard for HR (company-wide mental trends, high/low-risk teams, usage). Personal mental data is processed on-device and de-identified so it is never shared with the employer, and the company states it holds ISO 27001. Product surfaces include FAV (the Face & Voice AI diagnosis engine), an EAP counseling center, and the Clify organization-insight analytics. The public presence (clify.co.kr, an imweb-built marketing and account site) exposes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Kakao Entertainment
providers.description: Kakao Entertainment Corp. is the South Korean entertainment subsidiary of Kakao Corp., formed from the 2021 merger of Kakao Page and Kakao M. It operates three business lines — Story (Kakao Page and Kakao Webtoon serialized webtoon and web-novel platforms, plus the overseas Tapas and Radish properties), Music (the Melon streaming service and the StarShip, IST, EDAM and Antenna labels), and Media (film, drama and artist management). Its public machine-readable API surface is agent-native rather than REST: Melon publishes a first-party remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://mcp.melon.com/mcp, in beta, exposing 18 anonymously-introspectable tools for music search, official Melon charts, artist and album detail, genre browsing, personalized DJ Mallang recommendations, listening history and playlist/playback URL generation. Access is authenticated with OAuth 2.0 against the Melon Alliance Auth v3 platform, which publishes RFC 8414 authorization server metadata and an RFC 7591 dynamic client registration endpoint. Kakao Entertainment publishes no OpenAPI, no REST developer portal, and no SDKs; the corporate site and the Melon consumer properties carry no developer program. Kakao Corp's general developer platform at developers.kakao.com belongs to the parent company and is profiled separately as `kakao`.

providers.name: Newneek
providers.description: Newneek (뉴닉) is a South Korean knowledge and media platform that makes news and current events easy and fun to follow. Founded by Kim So-yeon and operated by Newneek Co., Ltd. from Seoul's Mapo district, the company is best known for its conversational email newsletter delivered by the mascot "Gosuni," alongside a mobile app, a Slack news bot, and active social channels. Newneek is a consumer content brand rather than an API producer: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. It appears in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company, and this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture. Enrichment probes found no OpenAPI, well-known, OAuth, MCP, or webhook surface to harvest.

providers.name: CLAP
providers.description: CLAP (주식회사 디웨일 / Dwhale Inc.) is a South Korean SaaS company offering an AI-powered, customizable performance management platform for enterprises. It covers the full performance lifecycle — multi-rater evaluations and calibration, OKR-style goal setting and alignment, continuous feedback and 1-on-1 meetings, and CLAP AI for diagnostics, feedback drafting, and automation — with tailored reporting and tool integrations. CLAP serves 1,000+ companies and claims to cut the HR time spent on performance management by up to 80%. The company is headquartered in Gangnam, Seoul, and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. CLAP publishes no public API or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and web properties.

providers.name: WE11DONE
providers.description: WE11DONE (pronounced "well done") is a Seoul-based fashion label founded in 2015 by Dami Kwon and Jessica Jung, the duo behind the Seoul concept boutique Rare Market. The brand fuses late-1990s and early-2000s streetwear and athleisure aesthetics into a globally distributed designer ready-to-wear line, sold through its own e-commerce storefront at we11-done.com and stockists worldwide. Surfaced as a consumer-sector portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed the company operates a direct-to-consumer retail website but publishes no developer API surface: no developer portal, API reference, well-known metadata, or llms.txt were found.

providers.name: Sankun
providers.description: Sankun (산군) is a South Korean construction-industry big data platform based in Seoul that aggregates and sells access to eight integrated construction databases covering roughly 280,000 construction companies, some 820,000 project sites, government e-procurement bids, contract awards, professional reputation reviews, and construction news. Alongside its web application and a construction sales CRM (Sankun Sales), the company markets a Sankun API (data.sankun.com) for programmatic access to its construction data, though public developer documentation is gated behind sales and login. Sankun is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: VCNC
providers.description: VCNC is a South Korean mobile technology company behind Between, a private messaging and photo-sharing app for couples, and TADA, a ride-hailing and mobility service operating in Korea. A 500 Global portfolio company, VCNC maintains an open source presence on GitHub, including Haeinsa, a multi-row transaction library for HBase published on Maven Central. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API client SDKs.

providers.name: Gridwiz
providers.description: Gridwiz Inc. is a South Korean clean-energy software and hardware company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Seoul. It operates one of Korea's largest demand response (DR) aggregation portfolios, gathering electricity that industrial and commercial customers curtail and selling it into the national power market, and it pairs that with energy storage (ESS), renewable energy / RE100 and PPA advisory, and an e-mobility line covering EV charging controllers, CCS communication modems (EVCC/SECC), bidirectional V2G chargers and the Skyblue consumer charging service. Its e-mobility products are built to the international EV charging standards DIN SPEC 70121, ISO 15118 (including 15118-20 AC/DC) and OCPP, and its demand response management system is described as OpenADR-based. Gridwiz sells energy services and certified hardware to utilities, EVSE suppliers and enterprises; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd. (주식회사 곳간, branded KOKKAN / 도심창고 곳간) is a South Korean urban self-storage and logistics operator headquartered in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. It rents managed storage units in five sizes (S, M, L, XL, XXL, from 1.0m cubes up to 2.0 x 2.0 x 2.0m) across 22 branches in Seoul, Busan, Incheon, Gyeonggi and Chungbuk, serving households storing seasonal appliances, clothing, bedding and baby goods as well as businesses storing samples, inventory, documents and office equipment. Customers select a branch, choose a unit size, pay and manage their contract through the KOKKAN mobile apps for iOS and Android, with recurring monthly card billing through a Korean payment gateway, long-term and promotional discounting, an address-rental (주소지 임대) product, and an optional pickup service for moving stored goods. The company also runs a franchise and partnership program for operators who want to open a KOKKAN branch. It was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this profile KokkanLogis publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or technical documentation — the product surface is a consumer website plus native mobile apps.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: B612
providers.description: B612 is a consumer selfie and beauty camera application for iOS and Android, published globally by SNOW Corporation and operated in mainland China as B612咔叽 (B612 Kaji) by Yiruike Information Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. The app combines a real-time beauty camera, AR stickers and scene effects, user-created and creator-published filters, and photo and video editing tools, and has been distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play since 2014. B612 is a mobile end-user product rather than an API provider: as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API artifacts on any of its web properties.

providers.name: Finda
providers.description: Finda (핀다) is a South Korean fintech company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Seoul that operates a licensed online loan-comparison and financial-product marketplace. Through its mobile app and website, Finda lets consumers compare loan products from 76+ financial institutions and 400+ products in about a minute, refinance existing loans ("갈아타기"), aggregate accounts and cards for asset management, run financial calculators (interest, DSR, year-end tax, mortgage eligibility), and monitor and manage their credit. Registered as a loan-brokerage/loan-collection corporation under Korea's Financial Services Act, Finda earns commissions from partner financial institutions rather than charging consumers. It reports 3.47M+ cumulative members and 256T+ won in managed loan assets, and is backed by 500 Global. Finda is a consumer B2C platform and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: lunchlab Corp.
providers.description: lunchlab Corp. (런치랩) is a Seoul-based corporate lunch subscription and delivery service that brings daily meals to office teams across South Korea. It offers two rotating meal lines — a traditional home-style Korean lunch box and a "Fresh Meal" line of poke bowls and sandwiches — with delivery and pickup included for a flat per-meal price, employees choosing their meals through a mobile app while administrators manage orders and billing from a web dashboard. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, lunchlab operates in the food-service / corporate-catering space and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Comento
providers.description: Comento is a South Korean career development and mentoring platform based in Seoul that connects job seekers with working professionals. The service offers a Q&A community and timeline for career discussions, free unlimited mentoring questions answered by industry practitioners, resume and cover letter (자기소개서) review, an AI resume analyzer, interview preparation, and job-focused educational programs including bootcamps (직무부트캠프) and classes for the Korean job market. It also runs corporate training and university affiliation partnerships. Comento operates as a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched with the domain and identity signals that are publicly observable.

providers.name: 21 Market
providers.description: 21 Market is the API Evangelist network profile for 주식회사 21세기전파상 (21st Century Electronics Shop Co., Ltd.), a South Korean consumer-electronics resale company that operates the Repercent (리퍼센트) service at repercent.com. Repercent buys used smartphones and mobile devices — iPhone, Galaxy, tablets, and laptops — from individual sellers, providing instant online price quotes, fast payment, and a simple pickup/logistics flow for secondhand device trade-in. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and was surfaced into the network as a venture portfolio lead. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile captures verified company identity, its live web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Veluga
providers.description: Veluga (Veluga Brewery Inc.) is a South Korean B2B alcohol wholesale distribution platform that connects hospitality business owners with liquor suppliers. Operating from Mapo, Seoul, the company runs a wholesale marketplace offering real-time wholesale pricing quotes for spirits and craft beverages, product recommendations for business owners, wholesale order facilitation, and partnership programs for distributors and catering services. Veluga positions itself as a transaction and information intermediary rather than a direct seller. The company began as a craft-beer and snack subscription service and is backed by 500 Global, Kakao Ventures, SparkLabs, HL Holdings, and Sema Investment. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures the company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: H2O Hospitality
providers.description: H2O Hospitality is a South Korea-based hospitality digital-transformation company that connects existing hotel and leisure systems rather than replacing them, streamlining operations from booking to checkout. Its products span three areas: Connect (cloud property-management tooling including Smart CRS, Smart RMS, and Smart FMS), Maximize (revenue and guest-engagement tools such as Smart D2C and AI-based CRM), and Transform (managed operations). It offers smart mobile check-in and automated inventory management, operates across nine countries in Korea, Japan, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, and is ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Woowa Brothers
providers.description: Woowa Brothers is the Seoul-based technology company behind Baedal Minjok (Baemin), South Korea's leading food delivery platform, alongside B-Mart quick commerce, Baemin Connect rider services, and robotics initiatives for serving and delivery robots. A subsidiary of Delivery Hero since 2021, the company runs a strong engineering culture through its Woowahan tech blog and first-party open-source libraries on GitHub (NestJS libraries, WoowahanJS, Redis tooling), but it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Levit
providers.description: Levit Inc. (레브잇) is a software company headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, best known for Alwayz (올웨이즈) — a mobile-first team-purchase commerce app launched in July 2021 that lets shoppers group together with other buyers to unlock prices below normal retail. Levit describes itself as building "a service that everybody uses everyday," and previously launched Ping in March 2021. The company runs the Alwayz Seller Center for merchants selling on the platform and publishes a seller-focused commerce blog. As of this profile Levit publishes no public developer API program, no API documentation or reference, no developer portal, and no SDKs — the enrichment pipeline probed the company and product domains and found no developer surface.

providers.name: Incheon Open Data
providers.description: Incheon Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for South Korea running DKAN.

providers.name: GeoGrid
providers.description: Geogrid Co., Ltd. is a South Korean smart-building water technology company behind BLOS ("Building Oasis"), an integrated building-level water purification and monitoring system. BLOS delivers drinkable water from every tap using chemical-free ionization to eliminate rust, scale, and biofilm, and pairs it with real-time monitoring of water quality, usage, carbon emissions, and consumption plus predictive analytics for pipe condition, contamination risk, and filter replacement. Geogrid targets schools, hotels and resorts, public institutions, and healthcare facilities, and offers a BLOS Care membership service. The company is based at Seoul Startup Hub Seongsu, holds 21 registered patents, and has been recognized with venture certification, ESG awards, and selection as a Korean representative for WSA 2026. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: MUSINSA
providers.description: MUSINSA is South Korea's leading online fashion platform, founded in 2001 by Cho Man-ho as a streetwear community and now operating a marketplace that connects more than 10,000 brands with over 16 million members. The company reported roughly USD 3.3 billion in GMV and USD 907 million in revenue for 2024, returned to operating profit, and is pursuing a KOSPI IPO. MUSINSA runs domestic and global storefronts (musinsa.com, global.musinsa.com), a partner/seller program for K-fashion brands, and an engineering organization that publishes on the MUSINSA tech blog. It has raised funding from investors including KKR, Sequoia/Peak XV (formerly Sequoia Capital China / HongShan) and IMM Investment. No genuine public product/developer API or OpenAPI-backed developer portal was found during enrichment; a corporate CMS Swagger UI at dev-api.corp.musinsa.com is an internal tool (its public spec still points at the Swagger petstore demo), so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Habitus Associates Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Habitus Associates Co., Ltd. is the company behind Artue (artue.io), an AI-powered online marketplace for original artworks by Korean and international artists. Artue lets collectors discover, purchase, and resell paintings, photography, sculptures, and prints, with natural-language search that finds works by mood, color, style, room type, or budget. The platform is explicitly agent-native: it publishes an llms.txt and ships a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT can search its collection directly. Backed by 500 Global and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from that portfolio.

providers.name: Boosters
providers.description: Boosters is a Seoul-based global commerce company and brand aggregator, founded in 2019, that acquires and accelerates the growth of emerging Korean direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, with a particular focus on K-Beauty. Boosters takes over small and medium-sized Korean brands that have strong product potential but struggle with marketing, distribution, and inventory management, then scales them across domestic and international commerce channels. Portfolio brands include Eqqualberry and Branden. The company raised a USD 10 million Series A round in 2022 with participation from Partech and other investors. Boosters is a consumer commerce operator rather than a developer platform, and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: INDEX Robotics
providers.description: INDEX Robotics is a South Korean humanoid robotics startup based in Seongnam (Bundang) building high-precision actuators and upper-body humanoid robots for high-mix, low-volume industrial work. Its core products are the IA Series, a family of high-precision actuators purpose-built for humanoid joints, and INDEX01, a compact upper-body humanoid prototype that deliberately foregoes a mobile base so it can slot into constrained factory workspaces for logistics handling, machining support, and precision assembly. The company treats joint precision, responsiveness under sustained repetitive motion, and long-run performance consistency as the core unsolved problems in humanoid commercialization. In February 2026 INDEX Robotics closed a $1M (KRW 1.5B) seed round led by Futureplay with Bass Ventures and 500 Global co-investing. This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Chaart
providers.description: Chaart (주식회사 차트, Chaart Inc.) is a Seoul-based art-trading and art-asset-management platform for South Korea's art collectors and investors. Its iOS and Android apps let collectors buy and resell artworks in the secondary market with transparent price/valuation information, automatic artwork matching, authenticity checks, secure delivery, and integrated payments. Chaart reports 5,000+ registered collectors and thousands of artworks traded, and raised pre-seed funding from 500 Global. Chaart is a consumer mobile app: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: MomMom
providers.description: MomMom (맘맘) is a South Korean consumer parenting and family-activity platform that helps parents discover places to go with their kids and products to buy for them. The mom-mom.net website and app curate kid-friendly destinations by region, family accommodation and resort deals, restaurant and class discounts, and community-driven product rankings (국민템랭킹) covering baby and childcare essentials, alongside parenting tips. It is a B2C curation, deals, and recommendation service, backed as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface is currently published (probed 2026-07-20).

providers.name: myBOX
providers.description: myBOX was an on-demand self-storage service founded in 2015 in Seoul, South Korea, and backed by 500 Global. It delivered storage boxes to a user's door for storing unused luggage and goods, offering free pickup and a range of container sizes for documents, clothes, and bulky items. The company has since permanently closed; its site (my-box.kr) no longer resolves and it exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: NOD Games
providers.description: NOD Games is a Seoul-based blockchain game studio founded in 2019 by CEO Chanki Lee, building entertaining game content and open, player-owned game platforms where gamers and communities own and trade in-game digital assets as NFTs. Its marquee titles are League of Kingdoms, a free-to-play 4X MMO strategy game with tradable Land NFTs and the LOKA token, and Crypto Sword & Magic, an RPG whose heroes, equipment, and pets are recorded on-chain with game logic running in smart contracts. The company is backed by a16z crypto. As of this enrichment pass NOD Games publishes no first-party developer program, public API, SDK, or GitHub organization; its official domain nodgames.com resolves to an unconfigured Wix parking page and the League of Kingdoms domain no longer resolves, so there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Pawdly
providers.description: Pawdly (포들리) is a South Korean pet e-commerce marketplace and mobile app operated by KCC I&C, offering pet product shopping across categories, saved/wishlist items, and pet-care service reservations, alongside pet-care tips and member benefits delivered through its app. KCC I&C operates as a payment intermediary and mail-order sales broker rather than the direct seller, with individual merchants fulfilling orders, shipping, and refunds. Pawdly was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass found a consumer web/mobile marketplace with no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Plantner Inc.
providers.description: Plantner Inc. (PLANTNER) is a South Korean biotechnology company specializing in the extraction and manufacturing of alginic acid, a biodegradable marine-derived biomaterial. Operating as a bio-industry platform provider, Plantner supplies alginic acid-based solutions across medical devices (wound dressings, nutraceuticals), pharmaceuticals (gastroprotective agents, drug-delivery systems), cosmetics (modeling masks, hydrogels), advanced biotech (bio-ink, organoids, delivery carriers), and agriculture (controlled-release fertilizers, mulching films, eco-friendly herbicides). Headquartered in Seoul with an R&D center in Suwon, the company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a materials/biotech manufacturer and does not currently publish a developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: RareLee
providers.description: RareLee (Rarelee) is a Seoul-based premium personal style consulting company founded in 2017, offering data-driven hair, makeup, and fashion analysis. Its consultants classify a client's face shape, features, and skeletal structure across millions of type combinations to recommend personalized hairstyles, makeup designs, and coordinated outfits, both online and in person. Rarelee serves celebrity clientele and has collaborated with brands such as Shinsegae and Marriott. It is a direct-to-consumer service with no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: RVDS Inc.
providers.description: RVDS Inc. is a South Korean food and beverage company that describes itself as growing into Korea's representative Multi-K-Food Brand Operator, building and operating a portfolio of consumer dining brands including Dodo Korea, Butai, and Salad Monster. Based in Cheongju-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, the company is backed by 500 Global. As a consumer food-brand operator it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this profile carries only identity and probed domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Storicity
providers.description: Storicity Inc. was a Seoul, South Korea-based travel-technology startup, founded around 2020 and backed by 500 Global, that built Yoda Trip (Korean brand "여다") — an AI-assisted consumer travel-planning mobile app offering customized itineraries and mobile audio guides for tourist destinations, shipped on iOS and Android. It was a consumer B2C mobile product rather than an API platform provider. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 (web search plus a live domain/TLS probe) found no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK packages, GitHub organization, or other developer surface. Public records indicate the Yoda Trip service was discontinued in April 2025 and the company is listed as out of business; the yodatrip.com domain still resolves but serves a broken TLS certificate.

providers.name: Theres Camping
providers.description: Theres (데얼스, Theres Co., Ltd.) is a South Korean e-commerce marketplace for outdoor and camping gear, where customers buy both new and second-hand equipment in one place. The platform aggregates brands and vendors (Grape Box, Camping Khan, Ridge Mountain Gear, Matador, and others), offering product search, a shopping cart, deal notifications, a community section, and vendor/product listing tools. Based in Seoul (Seocho-gu), Theres is a portfolio company of 500 Global. The company publishes a consumer web/app storefront and does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or integration surface.

providers.name: Ticketmonster
providers.description: Ticketmonster (TMON) is a South Korean e-commerce and social-commerce platform founded in 2010 as "Ticket Monster." Operating primarily at tmon.co.kr (the legacy ticketmonster.co.kr brand), TMON sells deals, daily bargains, fashion, travel, and a broad retail catalog to Korean consumers via web and mobile apps. It grew into one of Korea's leading online marketplaces and was later brought under the Qoo10 group. TMON is a consumer-facing retail/marketplace business; it does not publish a public developer program, API portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documented API surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed the absence of any public API surface.

providers.name: TimeBlocks
providers.description: TimeBlocks is a consumer calendar and personal scheduling mobile app developed by Day2Life Inc., a South Korean company backed by 500 Global. Marketed as Korea's #1 decoration calendar, it brings calendar, to-do, memo, and habit tracking together in a single view, with patented drag-and-drop time-block scheduling (US Patent 10,409,474 B2), roughly 1,000 customization items (themes, stickers, fonts), shared and group calendars with real-time notifications, seven home-screen widgets, and cloud sync across devices. It is a native iOS and Android app; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Tumblbug
providers.description: Tumblbug (텀블벅) is a South Korean reward-based crowdfunding platform for creators, where makers launch projects and backers pledge funds to bring creative works — comics, games, publishing, design, music, film and more — to life. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Tumblbug publishes a consumer-facing web platform (help center, creator guides, pricing/advertising, terms and privacy pages) but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or open API surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: BAYCON
providers.description: BAYCON Inc. is a Seoul, South Korea-based mobile connectivity company, founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global and Shorooq Partners (seed round, 2024). BAYCON operates a global data eSIM platform and a family of international communication apps: eSIM Easy (이심이지), which delivers multi-country data eSIM plans as a QR code within minutes of purchase; ModuCall (모두의 국제전화), affordable VoIP international calling that lets users place overseas calls using their domestic mobile plans; and BayTalk. The company partners with local network operators and global carrier infrastructure so international travelers and businesses can access local mobile networks without physical SIM cards, cut roaming costs, and stay connected across borders, and is expanding into travel content such as attraction tickets and transportation passes. BAYCON publishes consumer mobile apps rather than a public developer API surface.

providers.name: PeopleFund, Perfect Technologies
providers.description: PFC Technologies (formerly PeopleFund) is a Seoul, South Korea fintech company operating at the intersection of direct online lending and AI lending infrastructure. It runs two platforms: CPLE (Crople), an online investment-linked finance (온라인투자연계금융) service that matches retail investors with consumer and small-business loans, and AIRPACK, an AI-powered, no-code underwriting and loan operations infrastructure (AIRPACK-Lab for data analysis, model development and approval-rule tuning, and AIRPACK-Studio for model deployment, rule-set operation and performance monitoring) sold to savings banks and other lending institutions. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or partner API surface; AIRPACK integrations are handled through a direct sales/contact process. This record was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched as an API Evangelist network company profile.

providers.name: Playcurio
providers.description: PlayCurio is a Seoul-based educational technology company that builds AR (augmented reality) play-learning products for children, pairing physical educational tools with digital content. Its catalog includes AR titles such as Curio Safari, Phonics Pop, Dictionary Pop, and Math Mates, alongside a content-IP business spanning characters like Detective Pete, Dino Tales, and 100+ Curio Safari animals, plus B2B production services (character development, 2D/3D animation, UI/UX, and live-action video). PlayCurio is consumer- and partnership-facing and publishes no developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation. Surfaced via the 500 Global portfolio and enriched here; a domain-security probe of play-curio.com is the only technical artifact this pass produced.

providers.name: Socra AI
providers.description: Socra AI operates Socra Tutor (소크라 튜터), a Korean-market, AI-powered education service that describes itself as an intelligent AI answer-comparison service — students submit problems and Socra compares and evaluates candidate answers using AI to help them learn. It is a consumer-facing edtech mobile/web application rather than a developer platform; as of this profile no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation could be found. Socra AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Medir
providers.description: Medir is a South Korean digital-health company behind Medb (메듭), a non-face-to-face (telemedicine) and prescription-drug delivery platform that connects patients, doctors, hospitals and pharmacies. Through the Medb mobile app, patients receive 100% video consultations with physicians and have their prescribed medications delivered to their door — often within roughly 30 minutes to two hours — with no separate service fee beyond the standard consultation charge. Medir is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. The business operates as a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network pending any future API surface.
